This criminal revision has been filed seeking to set aside the order dated 24.11.2022 made in R.C.S.No.5 of 2019 by the learned Judicial Magistrate No.II, Gobichettypalayam concerning Crime No.268 of 2018 on the file of Kadathur Police Station, Erode District and to issue direction to convert the Protest Petition in R.C.S.No.5 of 2019 as private complaint and deal with the same in the manner known to law.

2.The case of the petitioner is that the respondents 2 and 3/ A1 and A2 availed credit facility to the tune of Rs.1,70,000/- from the petitioner Bank by mortgaging the property being commercial land and building of an extent of 3.24 acres comprised in S.Nos.214/4, Old No.289  items each of an extent of 1.62 acres.
The said mortgaged property had ACC roofed building with electricity and other amenities.

Owing to default to repay the loan, the defacto complainant/ petitioner Bank taken symbolic possession of the said property under Section 13(4) of SARFAESI Act on 23.06.2013 and the property was https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis subjected to auction on 15.12.2017 and on successful bidding sale amount was paid and subsequently sale certificate was issued by the Authorised Officer in favour of successful bidder and till such time registration process was pending and possession was not handed over to the bidder.
3.The further case of the petitioner is that on 25.06.2018, the petitioner happened to witness that the super structure in mortgaged property was demolished and upon enquiry, the said demolition alleged to have been taken place in the early morning on the said date.
Hence, complaint was lodged and FIR under Sections 420, 447 IPC and 3(1) of TNPPDL Act was registered as against the respondents 2 and 3/ accused.

Thereafter the final report referring the case as 'false' was filed and the petitioner filed protest petition, however, the final report referring the case as 'false' was accepted by the learned Judicial Magistrate No.II, Gobichettypalayam and the defacto complainant was permitted to prefer complaint under Section 200 of Cr.P.C., if aggrieved.

Challenging the same,
the petitioner has filed the present revision.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

4.The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner being the secured creditor, obtained order from the Court and took symbolic possession of the said property under Section 13(4) of SARFAESI Act on 23.06.2013, however, inorder to deprive the rights of the petitioner, the respondents 2 and 3 / accused demolished the super structure in mortgaged property.

The learned counsel further submitted that when possession was in the hands of the M/S.Bank Of India vs Inspector Of Police on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123186003/
2 petitioner, the respondents 2 and 3 do not have any right to demolish the building in the mortgaged property, however, the trial Court denied to take cognizance of the case.
5.In support of his contentions, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner relied upon the decision of the Apex Court reported in (2019) 8 SCC 27 [Vishnu Kumar Tiwari Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh] and the relevant portion reads as follows:

sentences.text: If a protest petition fulfils the requirements of a complaint, the Magistrate may treat the protest petition as a complaint and deal with the same as required under Section 200 read with Section 202 of the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Code.
In this case, in fact, there is no list of witnesses as such in the protest petition.
The prayer in the protest petition is to set aside the final report and to allow the application against the final report.

While we are not suggesting that the form must entirely be decisive of the question whether it amounts to a complaint or is liable to be treated as a complaint, we would think that essentially, the protest petition in this case, is summing up of the objections of the second respondent against the final report.

6.The learned counsel appearing for the respondents 2 and 3 submitted that as against the SARFAESI proceedings, A1 and Company filed W.P.No.30999 of 2023 and the Hon'ble Division Bench of this Court vide order dated 26.10.2023 made in W.M.P.Nos.30642 and 30644 of 2023 in W.P.No.30999 of 2023 directed the respondent therein including the petitioner herein to maintain status quo and the said order is still in force.

The learned counsel further submitted that when the status quo order is in force in respect of the very same property, forcing the law enforcing agency to take cognizance of the accused persons is clear contempt.
Further the law enforcing agency arrived at a conclusion that there is no prima facie material to hold https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis A1 and A2 committed the offence.
In any event, the petitioner cannot force the law enforcing agency to proceed with the investigation.

The learned counsel further submitted that if at all the petitioner is aggrieved, the petitioner can file private complaint under Section 200 of Cr.P.C. and further submitted that already the learned Judicial Magistrate No.II, Gobichettypalayam has granted liberty to the petitioner to file private complaint under Section 200 of Cr.P.C.
7.Heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, the learned Government Advocate (Crl.
Side) appearing for the first respondents and the learned counsel appearing for the respondents 2 and 3 and perused the materials available on record.

8.Perusal of records disclose that already A1 and Company filed W.P.No.30999 of 2023 before the Hon'ble Division Bench of this Court and the Hon'ble Division Bench of this Court has directed the petitioner to maintain status quo and the said order is still in force.

When the status quo order is in force in respect of the very same property, forcing the law enforcing agency to take cognizance of the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis accused persons is not sustainable one.
Further the law enforcing agency arrived at a conclusion that there is no prima facie material to hold A1 and A2 committed the offence.
In any event, the petitioner cannot force the law enforcing agency to proceed with the investigation.

If at all the petitioner is aggrieved, the petitioner can file private complaint under M/S.Bank Of India vs Inspector Of Police on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123186003/
3 Section 200 of Cr.P.C. or under Section 203 of the Bharathiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, and already the learned Judicial Magistrate No.II, Gobichettypalayam has granted liberty to the petitioner to file private complaint under Section 200 of Cr.P.C.

9.This criminal revision case is dismissed.
